{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=PCFG-derived+uncertainty+metrics+as+triggers+for+meta-reasoning+loops+in+AI+architectures&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1007/bfb0013954\", \"title\": [\"Reasoning with uncertainty in AI\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/bfb0013954\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1996]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-94-017-1743-4_3\", \"title\": [\"Temporal Semantics of Meta-Level Architectures for Dynamic Control of Reasoning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-017-1743-4_3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2001]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"title\": [\"An Engineering Framework for Self-Correcting Autonomous AI Agents: Mitigating Hallucinations and Reasoning Loops in Autonomous Engineering Workflows\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper presents TRACE (Trajectory Reliability and Correction Engine), a runtime self-correction framework for autonomous AI agents in engineering workflows. TRACE targets a reliability gap in multi-step tool-using agents, where unsupported claims, contradictions, repetitive loops, and tool-use anomalies can propagate across long execution trajectories. Existing self-correction methods typically rely on post-hoc reflection or a single intervention mechanism, but do not integrate continuous runtime monitoring, failure attribution, and adaptive recovery in one control layer. TRACE wraps a standard ReAct-style agent with four modules: a Trajectory Monitor, a Failure Attribution module, a Recovery Controller, and an Audit Layer for structured trace logging. We evaluate TRACE on a simulated enterprise incident-triage benchmark of 50 tasks with injected hallucination- and loop-inducing conditions across four difficulty levels. TRACE achieves 76.0% task success versus 68.0% for a self-reflection baseline and 62.0% for vanilla ReAct, while reducing hallucination incidence from 19.4% to 9.6% and loop frequency from 12.1% to 4.8%. The framework is intended for reliable, auditable autonomous execution in engineering environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5226493\", \"title\": [\"Synthetic reasoning - Designing AI Architectures Beyond Neural Networks with Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><div>\\n <p>Synthetic reasoning stands at the forefront of artificial intelligence innovation, proposing a paradigm shift through the fusion of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. Hybrid neuro- symbolic systems aim to overcome the inherent limitations of conventional AI architectures, offering a pathway toward enhanced interpretability, robustness, and common-sense reasoning — attributes that are critical for high-stakes applications in healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. This paper investigates the architectural design, practical applications, and ethical implications of these hybrid systems, highlighting their capacity to combine data-driven learning with structured, logic- based reasoning. While these architectures promise improved adaptability and decision transparency, they also present formidable challenges in scalability, complexity, and ethical governance. Addressing these obstacles is essential for developing AI systems that align with human values and societal needs. The study positions synthetic reasoning as an essential step toward bridging the divide between human cognitive flexibility and machine intelligence, paving the way for reliable and ethically resilient AI solutions.</p>\\n</div></jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5226493\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "bd0958705422a680aed6382cc89a32e6126662961c882956f3d9fb73b9245044", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1007/bfb0013954", "doi:10.1007/978-94-017-1743-4_3", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6759126", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.5226493"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1007/bfb0013954", "https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-017-1743-4_3", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6759126", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5226493"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
